title: Introducing All-in-One Compact: One Device for All Payments
summary: All-in-One Compact is a QR-first payment device that brings static QR, dynamic QR, card tap and card dip together in one compact device, at the cost structure
body_markdown:
It is 7:30 in the evening at a neighbourhood pharmacy. There is a small queue at the counter. One customer scans the QR code. The soundbox chimes. The next customer does the same.


Scan. Chime. Done.


The merchant barely has to think about the payment. Neither does the customer. Then the next person reaches for a card. For a moment, everything slows down.


The merchant looks around for the card machine. Maybe it is somewhere under the counter. Maybe it has not been charged. Maybe there is no card machine at all.


It is a small moment. But it reveals something larger about the way payments work across millions of retail counters in India.


QR has become the *default* . Cards have not disappeared. And merchants have been forced to choose between the two.


For a pharmacy, salon, minimart or neighbourhood store where most customers pay through UPI, paying a higher rental for an Android POS device can be difficult to justify. The card machine may only be needed a few times a day, while the QR code is used constantly.


So the merchant does what makes economic sense. QR stays on the counter. The card machine often does not.


The result is a payment setup shaped not by what the merchant wants to accept, but by what makes sense to pay for. That is the gap we wanted to solve. Not by asking merchants to change the way they already accept payments. But by designing a device around it.


### **Introducing Razorpay All-in-One Compact.**


All-in-One Compact is a QR-first payment device that brings static QR, dynamic QR, card tap and card dip together in one compact device, at the cost structure of a soundbox.


The idea is deliberately simple. Keep QR exactly where merchants want it: always visible and ready for everyday transactions. Then add card acceptance for the moments when customers need it.


So the same pharmacy counter that handles dozens of QR payments through the day can also accept a tap or dip when a customer reaches for a card. No second device. No separate card machine sitting idle. No change to the merchant’s everyday payment behaviour. The counter simply becomes ready for more.


Scan. Tap. Dip. One device for all payments.


That simplicity matters because small retail counters are already crowded. There are billing machines, product displays, cables, phones, QR stands and payment devices competing for space.


### The All-in-One Compact is built for that environment.


Its compact form factor is designed for high-density retail counters. A dual-screen interface gives both merchant and customer visibility into the transaction. Battery capacity comparable to Android POS devices supports everyday usage. And the static QR remains visible throughout, because QR is still at the centre of how these merchants get paid.


But the biggest change is not what sits on the counter. It is what the merchant no longer has to choose between.


All-in-One Compact offers POS-level payment acceptance at up to one-third the cost of an Android POS, making broader payment acceptance more viable for merchants with occasional card usage.


A merchant can remain QR-first without being QR-only. And that creates an equally important opportunity for banks.


Banks have already acquired large numbers of merchants in QR-heavy retail segments. But expanding card acceptance across that base has often meant deploying Android POS devices whose economics do not always match the merchant’s transaction mix.


A merchant who receives a handful of card payments every day does not necessarily need the same payment setup as a merchant processing cards continuously.


### All-in-One Compact gives banks another way to serve that merchant.


One that can help expand card acceptance across existing QR merchants, improve device utilisation and make merchant acquisition more viable across price-sensitive retail segments.


Think pharmacies. Salons. Minimarts. QSRs. Apparel stores. Clinics. Hardware stores. Mobile stores. Businesses where QR may dominate the day, but the ability to accept a card still matters when the moment arrives.


Because payment acceptance should not force merchants to choose between what customers want and what the economics allow. The best payment device is not always the one with the most capability. It is the one that fits the way the business actually runs.


That is what All-in-One Compact is built to do. Not replace QR. Not turn every merchant into an Android POS merchant. Simply take the payment behaviour that already works, and make it capable of doing more. Retail does not need another POS machine. It needs smarter payment acceptance.


Scan. Tap. Dip. One device for all payments. Compact structure. Affordable rates. Built for doing more.


**This is Razorpay All-in-One Compact.**
